displayQuote: Eighty percent of success is showing up

meta.title: Who really said "Eighty percent of success is showing up"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Woody Allen really said it: a 1989 letter to William Safire confirms "80 percent of success is showing up." The first known version (1977) said "life."
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Eighty percent of success is showing up'?
meta.ogDescription: Allen claimed it in writing in 1989. The earliest close match, from 1977, reads "Showing up is 80 percent of life", and both wordings trace back to him.

answer.label: Said by
answer.sourceLine: Allen’s own claim. In a letter quoted in William Safire’s New York Times language column of August 13, 1989, he wrote: “I did say that 80 percent of success is showing up.” The earliest close match Quote Investigator ↗ has found is from 1977. It is credited to Allen but uses “life” instead of “success.”

source.heading: Where Allen claimed it

docMeta.dd: Woody Allen’s letter to William Safire, quoted in Safire’s “On Language” column, New York Times

By 1982, as an epigraph in In Search of Excellence (Peters & Waterman)

source.excerpt: My observation was that once a person actually completed a play or a novel he was well on his way to getting it produced or published, as opposed to a vast majority of people who tell me their ambition is to write, but who strike out on the very first level and indeed never write the play or book. In the midst of the conversation, as I’m now trying to recall it, I did say that 80 percent of success is showing up.
trail: 1977: The earliest close match Quote Investigator ↗ has found is in the New York Times of August 21, 1977. In a joint interview with Allen, Marshall Brickman says: “As Woody says, ‘Showing up is 80 percent of life.’”
1982: The “success” wording, credited to Allen, appears as the epigraph to chapter five of In Search of Excellence, according to Quote Investigator ↗.

1989: Asked by William Safire which version is correct, Allen writes: “I did say that 80 percent of success is showing up.” Both this letter and the 1977 interview are listed under the Attributed heading on Wikiquote ↗.
2008: In an interview with Collider, Allen gives the other wording: “I made the statement years ago which is often quoted that 80 percent of life is showing up” (archived interview ↗).
source.excerptNote: Transcribed by Quote Investigator from the New York Times of August 13, 1989. Asked why he chose eighty, Allen said that “the extra syllable in 70 ruins the rhythm of the quote.”

author.name: Woody Allen
author.heading: About Woody Allen
author.bio: Woody Allen is an American comedian, writer and filmmaker. He co-wrote Annie Hall (1977) with Marshall Brickman, and it was in a joint interview with Brickman that year that the “showing up” maxim was first printed under his name. Allen later explained that the remark began as advice to young writers: most people who want to write never finish the play or the book.

misattribution.heading: The wording drifts, but the credit doesn't
misattribution.intro: This is one of the rare lines pinned on Woody Allen that really is his. What wanders is the wording: the percentage and the noun change as the line is retold.

items.why: This is the 1977 wording, spoken by Marshall Brickman, who credited it to Allen. Allen used it himself in 2008. See Quote Investigator ↗.
Brickman spoke the 1977 words in print, but he said “As Woody says.” He was quoting his co-writer, with Allen present at the interview (Quote Investigator ↗).

items.who: “Ninety percent of life is just showing up”
items.why: This version was printed in the Boston Globe in 1983. Safire reported in 1989 that President George H. W. Bush used it, crediting Allen (Quote Investigator ↗). In his reply, Allen said the figure was 80.

items.who: “99 percent of life is showing up”
items.why: This version was printed on a T-shirt described in the New York Times in 1978, again credited to Allen (Quote Investigator ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: The line is Allen’s. He confirmed the “success” wording in a 1989 letter and recalled the “life” wording in 2008. Which came first is not known: Quote Investigator ↗ notes he may have used “success” in an earlier interview that has not been found.

context.heading: Advice to young writers
lead: Allen explained the line to William Safire in 1989. It came from a conversation about advice to young playwrights: people who actually finished a play or a novel were well on their way to having it produced or published, while most would-be writers “strike out on the very first level.” In 2008 he made the same point to Collider, calling it “my biggest life lesson that has worked.”

By 1982 the “success” wording was the epigraph to the chapter called “A Bias for Action” in the business bestseller In Search of Excellence. That is one route by which it moved from show business into management and self-help writing.
detailsBody: Allen’s 1989 letter also says the figure “seems high to me today,” but that “it was more than 60.” He chose 80 because the extra syllable in 70 would spoil the rhythm. So the number was picked for rhythm, not measured.
The columnist Ellen Goodman had already corrected herself in 1988, writing that Allen said “80 percent of SUCCESS is showing up,” not “life.” See the chronology at Quote Investigator ↗.
context.pull: The extra syllable in 70 ruins the rhythm of the quote.
